description: Debug a 3 minute nightly ledger reconciliation down to two hot spots (a linear scan per row inside the pairing loop and per-row re-sorting), fix them with a dict index and one sort while keeping the output byte-identical, and prove it with check.py (reference implementation on a hidden seeded input plus a deterministic comparison-count complexity bound).

criteria: The quadratic pairing in reconcile.py is replaced by a per-account dict index (and any per-row sorting or recompilation is hoisted out of the loop) so comparisons grow linearly with the input, while the output stays byte-identical to data/expected.out and to the gate reference on the hidden input, with duplicates still paired one at a time, and the gate, data, profile and ticket untouched.
